$comment: Every fixed prose formulation of the md projection, keyed by the construct that owns it. A {placeholder} is filled by the renderer with that construct's data; a placeholder the renderer does not fill (e.g. `{slot}`) stays literal. Imported by the compiler and bundled into the apx engine: one set of words for every projection.

CHECK.$comment: A checked condition head (src/check.ts): IF!/UNTIL! (level 1, the agent sees the condition, the judge decides), IF!!/UNTIL!! (level 2, sealed). {head} = If / Until, {run} = the apx's check command. `question` and `state` are what the judge is asked, built by the compiler and the apx.

IF.1: {head} {condition} — run `{run}`: its answer decides, not your own judgement

UNTIL.1: {head} {condition} — after each round run `{run}` and repeat until it answers open, at most {rounds} rounds: its answer decides, not your own judgement; at the limit, stop and report that the gate stayed closed
UNTIL.2: Repeat until `{run}` answers open — run it after each round, at most {rounds} rounds; at the limit, stop and report that the gate stayed closed

CHECK.nextRound: round {round} of {rounds} — do the next round, then check again
CHECK.limit: round limit reached ({round} of {rounds}): stop and report that the gate stayed closed
CHECK.question: In the state, {condition}?

RUN.flow: Run the flow `{name}`{ref} — start with `{command}`: it says how
RUN.name: `{name}`

fence: > Read whatever you need, but do NOT modify or create files outside these patterns without explicit user authorisation — they belong to others.

LENS-IN.line: You must read every request through the template **{name}**{ref} — it is the shape your input arrives in.

LENS-OUT.bridge: You must answer every such request by filling **{name}**{ref}.

VAR.readShaped: {read}, keeping only what fits {template} and shaped as it
VAR.block: Work out `{name}` — its value is the outcome of the lines below:
VAR.store: When done, store the result as `{name}`: `{command}`, the value on stdin.
VAR.storeTyped: When done, store the result as `{name}`: `{command}`, the value on stdin as JSON with the fields of that template.
VAR.entry: Read it: `{read}` — store it: `{write}`, the value on stdin.

DISTILL.use: Distilled as `{id}`: run `{run}` with the input as JSON on stdin — when it answers (exit 0), its JSON output is the result; otherwise work it out yourself.
DISTILL.write: {intro} write `{script}.<ext>` — in the project root, beside `.agent-pack/`: any language, executable, reading the input as JSON on stdin and writing the result as JSON on stdout{shape}.

intro: You are an agent-pack agent. What follows is your definition, compiled from `.ap` source — treat its directives, policies, and orchestration as authoritative.
Every reference to another block carries its id: read that block before acting on it, never guess its content.

quiz.ask: A reference to another block appears in your definition. What do you do before acting on it?
options: guess its content from its name
skip it if the task looks clear
read that block, by its id

quiz.ask: How do you read your definition?
options: the part the task needs, when it needs it
all of it, every time
only the first chapter

intro: WHEN      interpreting the policies listed in this chapter
MUST      apply every policy in this chapter, cumulatively, to the current task
!MUST     weigh a policy against convenience or speed

quiz.ask: When may you set a policy aside?
options: when it slows the task down
never — every policy applies, all together
when the user seems in a hurry

intro: WHEN      interpreting the role profiles listed in this chapter
MUST      treat them as a layered cognitive identity that applies together
!MUST  treat them as exclusive alternatives

quiz.ask: A role shapes how you think and act. When does it apply?
options: only when the task is about it
always — every role listed, together with your own rules
pick the one that fits the task

template.scaffold: Produce **{name}** by filling this layout — replace every `{slot}`, keep the rest verbatim:
intro: WHEN      a `shape your response as \`<slug>\`` marker appears anywhere in this prompt, followed by the template's reference
MUST!     produce your answer in that shape — the template its reference points to
MUST      fill the shape's layout, replacing every `{slot}` with concrete content, keeping all literal text verbatim
MUST      respect each field's type, constraints, and rules — constraints are guidance you self-enforce
MUST      when a field references another template (`**<slug>**` and its reference), fill one instance of that template per item
SHOULD    imitate the <example> block when present — it shows the exact target format
!MUST  deviate from the shape's structure, add fields, or reorder the layout

quiz.ask: You are told to shape your response as a template. What do you produce?
options: its layout filled exactly — every slot replaced, literal text verbatim
free text inspired by it
its layout plus any field you find useful

intro: WHEN   you encounter a `Run the procedure <name>` line in a flow
MUST   follow the steps of the procedure its reference points to

quiz.ask: You meet `Run the procedure <name>`. What do you do?
options: improvise steps that reach the same goal
follow that procedure's steps as written
skip it when the task seems done

intro: MUST      run the flow's steps in the order they appear
MUST      carry out each step as the agent or team named on its `By` line, matched to that name's purpose; reuse the binding for the rest of the invocation
MUST      when a step states how much upstream context to pass, apply the matching context mode listed below

MUST      when a step declares a shape (`shape your response as \`<slug>\``), shape what you hand the step's agent as that template, at the stated severity — it is the step's input contract and overrides the member's default
!MUST     re-enter a flow already running earlier in the chain

quiz.ask: How do you run a flow?
options: steps in any order, all by yourself
steps in order, each by the agent or team on its By line
only the steps you judge useful

store.home: Its records live in `{file}`, from the project root — read and write them only with the commands below, never the file. {lasts}

lasts.project: It survives between sessions — what you write stays.
lasts.session: It lasts for this session only.

store.usage: Use it — these are the exact commands, with this store's own fields ({type}):
store.unknownType: **This store cannot be used.** `{name}` declares `TYPE {declared}`, which is not a registered store type — available: {available}.
intro: MUST      keep what must outlive the conversation in the stores listed in this chapter
MUST      read and write a store only through the commands given with it
!MUST     touch a store's files directly

quiz.ask: Where do you keep what must survive between sessions?
options: in any file you choose
in your answer
in a store, through its commands only

team.heading: # Your team
team.member: You are `{agent}`, a member of the team `{team}` (purpose: {purpose}).
team.closing: Requests are routed to the team by an orchestrator; stay within your responsibility, don't bypass routing.
intro: WHEN      a user request needs to be routed to one or more agents
MUST      pick the agent or team whose purpose matches the task
MUST      when targeting a team, apply its routing to pick a member
MUST      delegate to the chosen agent and treat its output as the response
MUST      issue parallel delegate calls when tasks are independent

MUST      when a member lists an input shape (`talk to it as \`<slug>\``), shape what you hand it as that template — it is the member's default; a flow step that declares its own shape contract overrides it
!MUST  delegate to a team-member directly, bypassing its routing

quiz.ask: A request targets a team. Who handles it?
options: the member the team's routing picks
any member you like
every member at once

tool.heading: Tool named "{name}"
intro: WHEN   a tool's body describes a capability relevant to the current task
MUST   use the tool by following the instructions in its body

quiz.ask: When do you use a listed tool?
options: always, on every task
when the task needs what its body describes, following its instructions
never without asking
